# 佛說觀無量壽佛經

**ID:** T0365
**Volume:** T12
**Category:** 寶積部類,淨土宗部類
**Original Category:** 寶積部
**Byline:** 宋 畺良耶舍譯
**Dynasty:** 劉宋
**Date:** 424–442
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0365

## Contributors
- 畺良耶舍 (A000004)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Guān wú liàng shòu fó jīng* in 1 fascicle is the *Visualization-of-Amitāyus Sūtra* — the third of the *Three Pure Land Sutras* (alongside [the Larger T0360](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0060) and [the Smaller T0366](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0072)). Translated by [畺良耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%95%BA%E8%89%AF%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) Kālayaśas (Sanskrit *Kālayaśas* "Time-Glory") in the early Liú-Sòng period, the work presents 16 visualisation-meditations (*shí liù guān* 十六觀) for cultivating contemplative-devotional engagement with Amitābha's Pure Land *Sukhāvatī*. The work became the principal contemplative-ritual basis of East Asian Pure Land practice and is the source of the doctrine of the *Nine Grades of Rebirth* (九品往生) — a hierarchical structure of rebirth-conditions that became foundational to Pure Land soteriology.

**Abstract**

The translation is conventionally datable to [畺良耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%95%BA%E8%89%AF%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) Kālayaśas's Liú-Sòng period (424 – 442 CE).

Modern scholarship (Pas 1995, [末木文美士](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%AB%E6%9C%A8%E6%96%87%E7%BE%8E%E5%A3%AB) Sueki Fumihiko, et al.) has raised significant questions about the work's textual history: the absence of a corresponding Sanskrit original (despite the existence of Sanskrit witnesses for both the Larger and Smaller *Sukhāvatīvyūha*) has led some scholars to argue that the *Visualization Sūtra* may be a Central-Asian or even Chinese-Buddhist composition rather than a translation of an Indic original. The traditional Indic-translation attribution is followed here as the canonical position.

The Taishō text (T0365) is established on a particularly rich apparatus including the *Liúbù běn* 流布本 ("Disseminated Edition") and the *Dūn* 敦 (Dūnhuáng) witnesses.
